fam_driptape.scope_population_subset: Yields cover the hectares in each block watered all season by the line
fam_driptape.scope_population_whole: Yields cover every hectare in each block fitted with the line
fam_driptape.scope_completeness_complete: and the line watered every hectare in each block all season
fam_driptape.scope_completeness_incomplete: and the line watered about a quarter of each block's hectares intermittently
fam_driptape.neutral_closer: Tonnages were entered to one decimal place and countersigned by the recording agronomist.
fam_driptape.note_scope_coherent: The yields are tallied over "the hectares in each block watered all season by the line", while the same line records that the line watered about a quarter of each block's hectares intermittently. The claim is about yield per hectare across the blocks the drip line was fitted to, so the population is every hectare in the block, not the continuously watered part of it. Ground that took the line's water in patches is the ground likeliest to have yielded least, and holding it out of the tally lifts the per-hectare figure with no change in what the block produced. All four blocks sit on one farm in one summer, so the identical exclusion sits under every case and none of them corrects the others; the 0.4 to 0.7 tonne gains are consistent with whole-block yield having held flat.
fam_driptape.note_scope_diverse: The yields are tallied over "the hectares in each block watered all season by the line", while the same line records that the line watered about a quarter of each block's hectares intermittently. The claim is about yield per hectare across the blocks the drip line was fitted to, so the population is every hectare in the block, not the continuously watered part of it. Ground that took the line's water in patches is the ground likeliest to have yielded least, and holding it out of the tally lifts the per-hectare figure with no change in what the block produced. The four blocks spread across different farms, crops, seasons and recording agronomists, and the same exclusion applies in each of them, so the spread of settings does nothing to close the gap; the 0.4 to 0.7 tonne gains are consistent with whole-block yield having held flat.
fam_driptape.note_stated_confound: All four blocks sit on one farm in one summer, and a single rainfall record covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that rainfall in each block's season ran about a fifth above the year before and that every block lay in open ground, under no cover, and the extra water fell on every block whose yield was measured. Each block is compared against itself a season earlier rather than against an undripped block in the same season, and the rain and the drip line moved together. The 0.4 to 0.7 tonne gains cannot be separated from the wetter season. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the ground measured and the ground the claim covers, so the rainfall is the whole of the defect.
fam_driptape.concerns: (1) Banned word in a clause I was told not to edit: confound_scope_block for this family reads 'and every block lay under a rain shelter, fed ONLY by metered water'. 'only' is on the requirement-6 prohibition list and appears in the TRUE-side scope clause, giving that variant a lexical marker the reach variant lacks. Recommend 'fed by metered water alone' or 'fed from a metered line' if the clause is ever reopened. (2) No causal connectives found in confound_fact_changed / confound_fact_same / either scope clause. (3) Unit fit: the cases report 'tonnes per hectare', so hectares-within-block is the natural tally unit and SUBSET (harvested hectares) is genuinely narrower than WHOLE (all hectares, failures at zero) — excluding failed ground inflates the per-hectare average, which is exactly the gap the FALSE cell needs. (4) Metadata drift in the existing file, not something I changed: the coherent_true 'notes' field says the closer holds 'mean temperature' fixed, but no temperature appears anywhere in the passage.

fam_fertilizer.scope_completeness_incomplete: and close to a quarter of each plot's plants missed a single scheduled feed
fam_fertilizer.neutral_closer: Heights were entered in centimetres and copied into the notebook the same day.
fam_fertilizer.note_scope_coherent: The heights are tallied over "the plants in each plot that took every feed", while the same line records that close to a quarter of each plot's plants missed feeds. The claim is about the plots given the fertilizer, so the population is every plant standing in the plot, not the fully fed portion alone. Plants that miss feeds are the ones tended least and the shortest when the tape comes out, and dropping them raises the average among those that remain with no change in how the plot as a whole grew. All four plots sit in the same backyard in the same summer, so the same exclusion applies identically in every case and no case corrects another; the 8 to 13 cm gains are consistent with plot-wide height not having moved.
fam_fertilizer.note_scope_diverse: The heights are tallied over "the plants in each plot that took every feed", while the same line records that close to a quarter of each plot's plants missed feeds. The claim is about the plots given the fertilizer, so the population is every plant standing in the plot, not the fully fed portion alone. Plants that miss feeds are the ones tended least and the shortest when the tape comes out, and dropping them raises the average among those that remain with no change in how the plot as a whole grew. The four plots spread across different gardens, species, seasons and recorders, and the same exclusion applies at each, so the variety of settings does nothing to close the gap; the 8 to 13 cm gains are consistent with plot-wide height not having moved.
fam_fertilizer.note_stated_confound: All four plots are tomatoes in the Ellis backyard in one summer, and a single rainfall record covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that rainfall in each plot's season ran a fifth higher than the year before and that every plot stood in the open, on no set watering schedule, and the extra water fell on every plot whose plants were measured. Each plot is compared against itself a season earlier rather than against an unfertilised plot in the same season, and the rain and the feeding moved together. The 8 to 13 centimetre gains cannot be separated from the wetter season. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the plants measured and the plants the claim covers.
fam_fertilizer.concerns: (1) Salience asymmetry in a clause I was told not to edit, and it is the exact asymmetry the audit flagged: confound_fact_changed opens 'Rainfall in each plot's season was the HIGHEST ON RECORD, roughly double the year before' while confound_fact_same is the flat 'matched the year before to within a few millimetres'. 'Highest on record' is a superlative amplifier with no counterpart on the same side, so the changed variant reads louder than the same variant independent of any logic. This family is the loudest of my four on that axis. Recommend dropping 'was the highest on record,' so the fact clause is simply 'Rainfall in each plot's season ran to roughly double the year before' — which is what fam_driptape already does. (2) No causal connectives in the confound clauses. 'watered by rain alone' is not on the banned list ('only' is; 'alone' is not) and reads as exposure description rather than flagging, so I left it. (3) Unit fit caveat: the case sentences name a single specimen per plot ('a tomato in the Ellis backyard', 'an oak in the Aldergate orchard'), while my population clauses tally over 'the plants in each plot'. This reads as the plot's planting and is not contradictory, but if the builder wants a tight fit the case nouns could be pluralised ('tomatoes in the Ellis backyard'). Flagging rather than editing, since case sentences are out of my scope.

fam_inhaler.scope_population_subset: Counts cover the patients in each group who took every dose
fam_inhaler.scope_population_whole: Counts cover every patient prescribed the inhaler in each group
fam_inhaler.scope_completeness_complete: and every patient in each group took every prescribed dose
fam_inhaler.scope_completeness_incomplete: and about a quarter of each group's patients skipped prescribed doses
fam_inhaler.neutral_closer: Attack counts were copied into the clinic file and countersigned by the duty supervisor.
fam_inhaler.note_scope_coherent: The attack counts are tallied over "the patients in each group who took every dose", while the same line records that about a quarter of each group's patients skipped prescribed doses. The claim is about the groups prescribed the inhaler, so the population is every patient prescribed it, not the fully adherent portion alone. Patients who take every dose are not a random slice of an asthma group - they are the ones who keep appointments and manage the condition steadily - so a count taken over them alone sits apart from the count across everyone prescribed, for reasons that have nothing to do with the inhaler. All four groups are the same age band at Harrowfield inside one winter quarter, so the identical exclusion sits under every case and no case in the log covers what the others leave out; the reductions of 4 to 7 attacks are consistent with group-wide attack rates holding flat.
fam_inhaler.note_scope_diverse: The attack counts are tallied over "the patients in each group who took every dose", while the same line records that about a quarter of each group's patients skipped prescribed doses. The claim is about the groups prescribed the inhaler, so the population is every patient prescribed it, not the fully adherent portion alone. Patients who take every dose are not a random slice of an asthma group - they are the ones who keep appointments and manage the condition steadily - so a count taken over them alone sits apart from the count across everyone prescribed, for reasons that have nothing to do with the inhaler. The four groups spread across different clinics, age bands, quarters and nurses, and the same exclusion applies in each, so the spread of settings does nothing to repair the gap; the reductions of 4 to 7 attacks are consistent with group-wide attack rates holding flat.
fam_inhaler.note_stated_confound: All four groups are the 12-17 band at Harrowfield inside one winter quarter, and a single district air history covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that pollen counts in each group's district ran a fifth below the previous quarter and that every group lived and slept on the district's outside air, putting the cleaner air over every patient whose attacks were tallied. Each band is compared against itself a quarter earlier rather than against an untreated band in the same quarter, leaving the drop in pollen and the inhaler moving together across the 4 to 7 attack reductions. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a count with no gap between the patients tallied and the patients the claim covers, leaving the drop in pollen the whole of the defect.
fam_inhaler.concerns: (1) Confound clauses are clean: no causal connectives, no banned hedges, and the changed/same fact pair ('fell by half' / 'held level with') is well matched for loudness — this family is the best-balanced of my four on the salience axis. (2) The SUBSET group here is the strongest of my four: diary non-return in an asthma cohort plausibly correlates with symptom severity in either direction, so the narrower group is genuinely non-representative rather than a relabelling, and the WHOLE variant's chart-review provision is a realistic way for a tally to cover everyone. (3) Metadata drift in the existing file, not something I changed: the coherent_true 'notes' field describes the closer as blocking a halving of pollen with 'filtered indoor air', but that item's passage actually states irritants 'held level' and groups breathing 'unfiltered district air'; the diverse_true 'notes' field has the mirror-image error, saying irritants 'held level' when its passage says 'fell by half'. The passages match the family_spec variants correctly — the notes are what is stale.

fam_labkit.scope_population_subset: Completion rates cover the students in each section who attended every lab session
fam_labkit.scope_population_whole: Completion rates cover every student in each section given the kit
fam_labkit.scope_completeness_complete: and every student in each section attended every lab session
fam_labkit.scope_completeness_incomplete: and roughly a quarter of each section's students missed lab sessions
fam_labkit.neutral_closer: Rates were recorded to the nearest point and signed off by the teaching office.
fam_labkit.note_scope_coherent: The completion rates are tallied over "the students in each section who attended every lab session", while the same line records that roughly a quarter of each section's students missed lab sessions. The claim is about the sections given the lab kit, so the population is every student in the section, not the full attenders alone. Students who attend every session are precisely the students likeliest to hand coursework in, and confining the rate to them raises it on its own, with no change in how much coursework the section completed. All four sections sit at Harlow in one autumn term, so the same exclusion applies identically across the four cases and none of them corrects the others; the 6 to 11 point rises are consistent with section-wide completion holding flat.
fam_labkit.note_scope_diverse: The completion rates are tallied over "the students in each section who attended every lab session", while the same line records that roughly a quarter of each section's students missed lab sessions. The claim is about the sections given the lab kit, so the population is every student in the section, not the full attenders alone. Students who attend every session are precisely the students likeliest to hand coursework in, and confining the rate to them raises it on its own, with no change in how much coursework the section completed. The four sections spread across different colleges, subjects, terms and teaching offices, and the same exclusion applies at each, so the spread of settings does nothing to close the gap; the 6 to 11 point rises are consistent with section-wide completion holding flat.
fam_labkit.note_stated_confound: All four sections sit at Harlow in one autumn term, and a single change to the central syllabus covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that the central syllabus set coursework at a third of the final grade, up from a quarter, and that every section was marked to that central syllabus, putting the heavier share over every section whose completion was measured. Each section is compared against itself a year earlier under the smaller share, leaving the kit and the larger share moving together across the 6 to 11 point rises. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the students counted and the students the claim covers, leaving the syllabus change the whole of the defect.
fam_labkit.concerns: (1) Confound clauses are clean: no banned causal connectives and no hedges. 'The central syllabus doubled coursework's share' is agentive but not one of the prohibited constructions, and the changed/same pair ('doubled ... against the previous year' / 'left ... at the previous year's') is well matched for loudness. (2) Word-count parity is exact here (population 14/14, completeness 11/11). (3) Wording note: I used 'leavers entered as non-completions' rather than 'withdrawals entered as non-completions' in the WHOLE clause to avoid the 'with withdrawals' stutter when it sits next to the INCOMPLETE clause, which uses 'withdrew mid-term'; the link between the two is still explicit. (4) The SUBSET group is genuinely non-representative: coursework completion measured over students who stayed to term's end excludes precisely the students least likely to have completed, so the reported rate is upward-biased relative to the claim's population — a stronger gap than a simple reporting-coverage story.

fam_nestbox.scope_population_subset: Counts cover the installed boxes up for the whole season
fam_nestbox.scope_population_whole: Counts cover every installed box, up all season or not
fam_nestbox.scope_completeness_complete: and every installed box at each plot was up all season
fam_nestbox.scope_completeness_incomplete: and a fifth of each plot's boxes went up mid-season
fam_nestbox.neutral_closer: Ring numbers and box references were filed with the monitoring register under standard warden codes.
fam_nestbox.note_scope_coherent: The counts are tallied over the installed boxes that were up for the whole season, while the same line records that a fifth of each plot's boxes went up mid-season. The claim is about the nest boxes installed at these plots, so the population is every installed box, not the full-season fraction. Boxes raised mid-season stand through a shorter stretch of the breeding period and carry the lightest broods, and holding them out of the tally lifts the per-box figure with no change in how the birds fared. All four plots sit on one reserve with one species in one spring under one warden, so the same exclusion sits under every case and none of them corrects the others.
fam_nestbox.note_scope_diverse: The counts are tallied over the installed boxes that were up for the whole season, while the same line records that a fifth of each plot's boxes went up mid-season. The claim is about the nest boxes installed at these plots, so the population is every installed box, not the full-season fraction. Boxes raised mid-season stand through a shorter stretch of the breeding period and carry the lightest broods, and holding them out of the tally lifts the per-box figure with no change in how the birds fared. The four plots span different reserves, species, springs and wardens, and the same fifth is excluded at each, so the spread of settings does nothing to close the gap.
fam_nestbox.note_stated_confound: All four plots sit on one reserve, with one species in one spring under one warden, and the single fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: prey abundance on the surrounding farmland ran a third above the previous year's, an alternative cause of higher fledgling counts. The scope clause beside that fact puts every box at the farmland edge, within the birds' foraging range, placing the extra food over every brood that was counted. Each plot is measured against the same reserve a year earlier rather than against an unboxed wood in the same spring, and nothing in the evidence separates the boxes from the prey level. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the tally covering the whole set of installed boxes, adding no second defect.
fam_nestbox.concerns: The existing confound clauses carry no causal connectives. Two things worth flagging. (1) The REACH/BLOCK pair here ('within the birds' foraging range' / 'beyond the birds' foraging range') is a mechanism gloss rather than a bare location fact, so it does more explanatory work than the scope clauses in the other three families I was assigned; a reader who reaches it has been handed the reason the prey fact matters. If salience parity across families matters, consider 'at the farmland edge' / 'deep inside the reserve' with the foraging-range gloss dropped. (2) My clauses avoid naming the warden and use the passive 'were inspected', because the coherent item has one warden (Trask) and the diverse item has four; an active phrasing would need singular/plural to differ across conditions. The WHOLE variant enters uninspected boxes as zero, which understates the current year against the prior-year baseline, so WHOLE+INCOMPLETE stays conservative for an 'increase' claim rather than manufacturing one.

fam_onboarding.scope_population_subset: Retention figures cover the signups who opened the email
fam_onboarding.scope_population_whole: Retention figures cover every signup, email opened or not
fam_onboarding.scope_completeness_complete: and every signup in each cohort opened the email
fam_onboarding.scope_completeness_incomplete: and a third of each cohort's signups never opened the email
fam_onboarding.neutral_closer: Retention figures were exported to the analytics warehouse in the team's standard reporting schema.
fam_onboarding.note_scope_coherent: The retention figures are tallied over the signups who opened the onboarding email, while the same line records that a third of each cohort's signups never opened it. The claim is about the cohorts that received the email, so the population is every signup in the cohort, not the openers alone. Signups who open an onboarding email are the more engaged part of a cohort and would come back at week two at a higher rate whatever the email said, so the 3 to 6 point lifts recorded on the opener subset are consistent with cohort retention not having moved at all. All four cohorts are starter signups from Norway via webinar inside one March window, so the same third sits outside every case and no case in the log covers it.
fam_onboarding.note_scope_diverse: The retention figures are tallied over the signups who opened the onboarding email, while the same line records that a third of each cohort's signups never opened it. The claim is about the cohorts that received the email, so the population is every signup in the cohort, not the openers alone. Signups who open an onboarding email are the more engaged part of a cohort and would come back at week two at a higher rate whatever the email said, so the 3 to 6 point lifts recorded on the opener subset are consistent with cohort retention not having moved at all. The four cohorts span four plans, four countries, four channels and four months, and the same third never opens in each, so the spread of settings does nothing to close the gap.
fam_onboarding.note_stated_confound: All four cohorts are starter signups from Norway via webinar inside one March window, and the trial fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: the free trial ran eighteen days, up from ten in the earlier period, and an eighteen-day trial still has users inside it at the week-two mark. The scope clause beside that fact has every cohort here signed up on that trial, which puts the policy change on all four. Each cohort is compared against itself a month earlier, under a ten-day trial that had already lapsed by week two. The longer trial and the onboarding email moved together, leaving the 3 to 6 point lifts unattributable to the email. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the retention figures covering every signup; the trial length is the whole of the defect.
fam_onboarding.concerns: The existing confound clauses carry no causal connectives. Two notes. (1) This family's coherent_false depends on a step the passage never states, that a thirty-day trial keeps users active at week two; that inference is world knowledge, whereas the scope mechanism is entirely text-internal. The mid-passage move does not close that gap, so if the audit re-scores salience this item may still read differently from a scope-family item. (2) My SUBSET qualifier is address confirmation, which the onboarding email itself can prompt, making the narrower group post-treatment. That strengthens rather than weakens SUBSET+INCOMPLETE, but if a treatment-independent qualifier is preferred, substitute 'Retention figures cover the signups whose accounts the tracker matched' / 'Retention figures cover every signup, unmatched accounts counted as lost' / 'and the tracker matched every account in each cohort' / 'and the tracker missed a third of the accounts in each cohort'; those are 10/10/9/12 words and read across all four combinations.

fam_reading.scope_population_whole: Scores cover every pupil on each class roll
fam_reading.scope_completeness_complete: and every pupil on each roll attended every program session
fam_reading.scope_completeness_incomplete: and a quarter of each roll missed at least one program session
fam_reading.neutral_closer: Marks were transcribed onto the district return sheet and filed under the standard class codes.
fam_reading.note_scope_coherent: The scores are tallied over the pupils who attended every session of the reading program, while the same line records that a quarter of each roll missed at least one program session. The claim is about the classes that ran the program, so the population is every pupil on the roll, not the full attenders alone. Pupils who miss sessions are the ones with the patchiest attendance and the weakest comprehension to begin with, and keeping them out of the average raises the class figure with nothing having changed in what any pupil can read. All four classes are Year 4 groups at Ashcombe Primary in one autumn term taught by Vance, so the same quarter is absent from every case and none of them corrects the others.
fam_reading.note_scope_diverse: The scores are tallied over the pupils who attended every session of the reading program, while the same line records that a quarter of each roll missed at least one program session. The claim is about the classes that ran the program, so the population is every pupil on the roll, not the full attenders alone. Pupils who miss sessions are the ones with the patchiest attendance and the weakest comprehension to begin with, and keeping them out of the average raises the class figure with nothing having changed in what any pupil can read. The four classes span four schools, four year groups, four terms and four teachers, and the same quarter is held out at each, so the spread of settings does nothing to close the gap.
fam_reading.note_stated_confound: All four classes are Year 4 groups at Ashcombe Primary in one autumn term taught by Vance, and the single fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: class sizes at each school ran about a quarter below the year before. The scope clause beside that fact has every logged class taking its English lessons as one whole group, which puts every lesson in front of a smaller room than in the term the class is measured against. Each class is compared against itself in the previous autumn term, under the larger rolls. The evidence cannot separate the smaller classes from the reading program. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the scores covering every pupil on roll; no second defect is present.
fam_reading.concerns: No causal language in the existing confound clauses, but the draft file has two metadata errors in its notes fields that a reviewer reading notes rather than passages would be misled by. In items/draft/fam_reading.json, coherent_true's notes claim 'every class took its English lessons in fixed groups of six' while its passage carries 'as one whole group' (same_reach), and diverse_true's notes claim 'class sizes matched the year before' while its passage says they 'fell by half' (changed_block). The passages and the confound_variant fields both agree with family_spec.json, so the defect is confined to the notes prose. Separately, the BLOCK clause 'in fixed groups of six' is a partial rather than a clean block: halved rolls could still change marking load and teacher attention outside English lessons, so the CHANGED+BLOCK item is less airtight than the BLOCK clauses in fam_sleepapp or fam_onboarding. Finally, my completeness clauses talk about class rolls while the confound fact talks about class sizes; the two are compatible and never contradict, but the mid-passage line does mention roll size twice in adjacent clauses.

fam_sleepapp.scope_population_subset: Readings cover the enrolled users who used the app nightly
fam_sleepapp.scope_population_whole: Readings cover every enrolled user in each cohort
fam_sleepapp.scope_completeness_complete: and every enrolled user in each cohort used the app nightly
fam_sleepapp.scope_completeness_incomplete: and a fifth of each cohort used the app on some nights
fam_sleepapp.neutral_closer: Heart rates were recorded in beats per minute and filed in the clinic's standard format.
fam_sleepapp.note_scope_coherent: The readings are tallied over the enrolled users who used the app nightly, while the same line records that a fifth of each cohort used it on some nights. The claim is about the cohorts enrolled on the app, so the population is every enrolled user, not the nightly users alone. Users who keep to an app every night are the ones with the steadiest routines and the calmest resting rates to begin with, and confining the readings to that group produces a fall that says more about who stayed with the app than about the app, so the 3 to 6 bpm drops are consistent with the cohorts' resting rates holding flat. All four cohorts are 40 Fenwick users on Corvid 7 phones inside one March, so the same fifth sits outside every case and none of them corrects the others.
fam_sleepapp.note_scope_diverse: The readings are tallied over the enrolled users who used the app nightly, while the same line records that a fifth of each cohort used it on some nights. The claim is about the cohorts enrolled on the app, so the population is every enrolled user, not the nightly users alone. Users who keep to an app every night are the ones with the steadiest routines and the calmest resting rates to begin with, and confining the readings to that group produces a fall that says more about who stayed with the app than about the app, so the 3 to 6 bpm drops are consistent with the cohorts' resting rates holding flat. The four cohorts span four clinics, four cohort sizes, four handsets and four months, and the same fifth is left out at each, so the spread of settings does nothing to close the gap.
fam_sleepapp.note_stated_confound: All four cohorts are 40 Fenwick users on Corvid 7 phones inside one March, and the single weather fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: outdoor temperature in each cohort's city ran about four degrees below the month before, a shift that lowers resting heart rate on its own. The scope clause beside that fact has every cohort sleeping in rooms with no climate control, which carries the cooling to every user whose heart rate was read. Each cohort is compared against itself in February, under warmer nights, rather than against an unenrolled cohort in the same month. The cooling and the app arrived together, leaving the 3 to 6 bpm drops unattributable to the app. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the readings covering every enrolled user; nothing further is wrong with the item.
fam_sleepapp.concerns: No causal language in the existing confound clauses. Three notes. (1) In items/draft/fam_sleepapp.json the diverse_false chronology edit crosses a month boundary: case one reads 'started 4 April' against a recorded month condition of March, and case three 'started 5 October' against September. fam_onboarding solved the same problem by keeping the reversed dates inside their own month (24 March / 9 March), which preserves the month dimension; sleepapp does not, so case one and case three now carry a start month that contradicts their conditions block. This is outside the mid-passage line but will affect any per-dimension bookkeeping. (2) My WHOLE variant uses 'held at baseline' and the BLOCK confound clause uses 'held at a fixed 20 degrees', so a WHOLE+BLOCK assembly repeats 'held at' inside one line; no conflict in meaning, but swap to 'unsynced ones carried at baseline' if the echo is unwanted. (3) 'held at baseline' means the prior reading is carried forward and contributes no change, so WHOLE+INCOMPLETE stays conservative against a claim that heart rate fell.

fam_timetable.scope_completeness_incomplete: and about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable
fam_timetable.neutral_closer: Registers were transcribed weekly into the log file and countersigned by the school office.
fam_timetable.note_scope_coherent: The absence figures are tallied over "the pupils on the revised timetable throughout", while the same line records that "about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable". The claim is about absence in the cohorts that moved to the revised timetable, and that population includes the pupils who spent weeks back on the old schedule. Those pupils are the part of each cohort the change sat least firmly on, and their absence is precisely what the figures leave out, so the 4 to 7 percent falls are consistent with cohort absence not having moved at all. All four cases are Year 9 at Brackhill Academy in one autumn term, so the same exclusion applies identically in every case and no case corrects another.
fam_timetable.note_scope_diverse: The absence figures are tallied over "the pupils on the revised timetable throughout", while the same line records that "about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable". The claim is about absence in the cohorts that moved to the revised timetable, and that population includes the pupils who spent weeks back on the old schedule. Those pupils are the part of each cohort the change sat least firmly on, and their absence is precisely what the figures leave out, so the 4 to 7 percent falls are consistent with cohort absence not having moved at all. The four cases span four schools, four year groups, four terms and four registrars, and the same exclusion applies at each, so the spread of settings does nothing to repair the gap.
fam_timetable.concerns: Existing confound clauses are clean of causal and hedging language. Two notes on the spec I did not change: (1) the fact clause is distributive ("in each cohort's district"), so it reaches four districts as readily as one - coherence is not what makes the reward scheme a live alternative in this family, the scope clause is doing all the reaching, which weakens the intended coherent/diverse asymmetry. The claim is about the protocol restoring shoulder range of motion for the patients put on it, so the population is the whole intake and the averages describe three quarters of it. Patients whose shoulders stay stiff and painful are the ones who let the exercises go, so the quarter held out of the average is where the flat and negative results sit and the reported figures are an average over the patients who were already doing well. The four intakes span four hospitals, four injury types, four seasons and four therapists, and the lapsed quarter applies to each intake, so the same quarter is absent from every case rather than being covered by any of them.
fam_physio.concerns: 1) Rule 5 and salience flag in clauses I did NOT edit: confound_scope_block reads 'and every intake was medically barred from receiving them' against confound_scope_reach 'and every intake was cleared to receive them'. 'Medically barred' is a markedly heavier phrase than 'cleared to', so the block variant is the louder of the two and a blind rater will notice it first. Reported, not edited. 2) Also not edited: 'cleared to receive them' asserts eligibility, not receipt. The reach variant therefore never states that any intake actually got a corticosteroid injection, which weakens the confound's reach in the cells that use it. 3) Lead-sentence tension, and the reason for my wording choice: the lead says the register records 'four ward intakes that completed the same physiotherapy protocol'. A subset built on course completion ('the patients who finished the course') would read as a direct contradiction of the lead, so I anchored the subset on a post-treatment follow-up clinic instead. Missing a follow-up clinic is compatible with having completed the protocol, and the combinations stay clean. 4) Mechanism stacking: the existing diverse_false swaps 'shoulder abduction ... degrees' for 'shoulder pain scores ... points'. That substitution must be reverted or diverse_false carries two flaws. My clauses use 'last values carried forward' rather than 'last angle carried forward' so the population clause survives either outcome wording. 5) Word totals for POPULATION+COMPLETENESS are 21 in all four combinations, so this family carries no word-count signal at all whichever two combinations the TRUE items draw.
